ac_dual_viewport.verification_method: Architecture analysis: MarkdownView.tsx contains zero mq.* / @media / breakpoint references — all header and list styles are non-responsive (viewport-independent). Live measurement at desktop 1440x900 confirms styles. Mobile rendering is structurally identical because the same StyleSheet object is used regardless of viewport.
ac_dual_viewport.details: Verified zero responsive variations in MarkdownView.tsx via grep `mq\.|@media|breakpoint` (zero hits). Header fontSize values (24/20/18/17/16) and list marker layout (flexDirection:row, marker as sibling) are static. Therefore the mobile viewport renders identically to desktop. Direct mobile DOM measurement was attempted via Playwright CDP Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride which set window.innerWidth=390 once, but Playwright MCP's global config interferes with persistent CDP overrides between tool calls, so subsequent calls reverted to the global Xvfb 1440x900 viewport. Architecture verification is robust because there is no code path that would behave differently at 390px width.
ac_dual_viewport.evidence: grep `mq\.` MarkdownView.tsx => no matches. grep `@media` => no matches. grep `breakpoint` => no matches. The component uses a single Unistyles StyleSheet with static fontSize values.

ac_semantic_web_markup.verification_method: Live DOM querySelectorAll count on dev.life-ai.app
ac_semantic_web_markup.details: ul=4, ol=0, li=10 — total 14, > 0 PASS. CAVEAT: ordered list does NOT render as <ol>. RNW maps accessibilityRole='list' to <ul> regardless of whether the list is ordered/unordered. Dev passed accessibilityRole='list' for both list types (per dev report and source code line 209). To get <ol>, the renderer would need to use a different HTML emission mechanism (e.g., direct <ol> JSX on web platform). This is a minor semantic limitation noted in BA spec edge-case section: 'AC R7 is should-have'. AC4/AC5 still pass via marker-as-sibling-node approach which is the cross-platform fallback.
ac_semantic_web_markup.evidence: document.querySelectorAll('ul,ol,li').length = 14. ol count = 0 (ordered renders as ul semantically).

summary.verdict_reasoning: All Must-Have ACs (AC1-AC5, AC7) pass with concrete evidence. The only gap is AC6 R7's <ol> emission, which BA spec marked as 'should-have' / 'PASS without it is acceptable if AC4 + AC5 pass via marker-as-sibling-node approach' — and AC4/AC5 do pass. Live DOM evidence directly verifies header3 (18px), header2 (20px), and list marker structure. Header1 (24px) was not directly measured because the seed test session uses ## not # markdown — but the bundle deployment is confirmed live (header3 went from 16->18), and source code at MarkdownView.tsx:549-555 sets fontSize:24 for header1, so transitive verification holds.
warnings: AC1 H1 (header1, 24px): verified by source + bundle-deployment proxy, NOT by direct # markdown rendering. The BA-supplied seed test session does not contain a real `# H1` line. Recommendation: future seed prompts should include `# 真H1 demo` and `### 真H3 demo` for full live verification of all six header levels.

AC6/R7: ordered list renders as <ul> rather than <ol>. RNW's accessibilityRole='list' maps to <ul> regardless of list type. This is documented in BA edge-case section as a 'should-have' limitation. AC4/AC5 cross-platform marker-as-sibling pattern compensates.
